business_scope.primary_industry_name: Cloud Vulnerability Scanning and Penetration Testing SaaS

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Marshall Islands (Unitary national jurisdiction; corporate registry administered in Majuro)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid — Common Law corporate tradition modeled on the Delaware General Corporation Law, blended with statutory registry requirements and Marshallese customary law for land matters
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Compact of Free Association between the United States of America and the Republic of the Marshall Islands (1986; Amended 2003)
Agreement for the Implementation of Article IV of the Compact of Free Association (U.S.–RMI tax and financial implementation agreement)
No comprehensive income tax treaty (DTAA) is currently in force for the Marshall Islands

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Primary statutes: (1) Business Corporations Act 1990, Title 51 of the Marshall Islands Revised Code (51 MIRC) §§ 101 et seq., as amended, including § 103 (name reservation), § 13 (registered office), § 14 (registered agent), and the confidential Beneficial Ownership Register amendment obligations; (2) the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism Act 2012, as amended (AML/CFT Act 2012), administered by the Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) of the Republic of the Marshall Islands; (3) the Financial Transactions Reporting Regulations; (4) the FIU consolidated AML/CFT guidance and the Asia/Pacific Group on Money Laundering (APG) mutual-evaluation framework.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access — The Marshall Islands Beneficial Ownership Register is confidential and non-public; access is granted exclusively to the Registrar of Corporations, the FIU, domestic law-enforcement agencies, and competent tax authorities under international exchange-of-information arrangements. Nominee arrangements are not statutorily prohibited but are strongly unattractive: nominee shareholders and directors must disclose the underlying beneficial owner to the Registered Agent and the confidential register at the 25% threshold.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Certified True Copy issued by the Registrar of Corporations)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Corporations, Ministry of Finance, Republic of the Marshall Islands
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (RMI Ministry of Foreign Affairs; RMI is a Contracting State to the Hague Apostille Convention)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing for the Business Corporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Corporations, Ministry of Finance, Republic of the Marshall Islands

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney appointing the RMI Licensed Registered Agent and corporate counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the UBO's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization by the competent authority of the document's country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Beneficial Ownership Declaration and UBO natural-person identification affidavit (passport and proof of address attached)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the UBO's country of residence, or the Registered Agent's compliance officer where notarization is waived under AML/CFT Act 2012 risk ratings

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certified passport copies and utility/bank statement proof of address for all directors, shareholders and ultimate beneficial owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public or competent public authority of the document's country of origin

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based customer due diligence under the AML/CFT Act 2012 and FIU guidance: screen all directors, shareholders, authorized signatories, and UBOs at the 25% threshold against (i) the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions lists (1267/1989 ISIL and Al-Qaida; 1988 Taliban), (ii) the OFAC SDN and CAPTA lists applied through USD correspondent banking, (iii) the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions list, and (iv) APG and domestic RMI advisories. Senior foreign political figures, domestic PEPs, family members, and close associates require automatic flagging, senior-management approval, enhanced monitoring, and source-of-funds/source-of-wealth verification. Any sanctions hit or adverse media finding is a reportable event to the RMI Financial Intelligence Unit.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registrar of Corporations – Business Registry, Ministry of Finance, Republic of the Marshall Islands. No public self-service portal; name clearance and reservation are submitted electronically through FIU-licensed RMI Registered Agents using the official Registry filing system. Name availability searches may be requested through the Registered Agent channel.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Official languages are Marshallese and English. Corporate names must be expressed in Latin/Roman characters; no mandatory Marshallese transliteration. Each name must include a statutory corporate designator such as Corporation, Incorporated, Limited, Company, or an accepted abbreviation (Corp., Inc., Ltd., Co.). Marshallese diacritics, if used, are normalized to ASCII in the register. Names must be distinguishable from all existing domestic and foreign registered entities.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Government / National / Commonwealth / State / Municipal (implied RMI state connection)
Marshall Islands (use of the country name requires Registrar consent)
Foundation / Society / Council / Commission / Club / Organization / Charity (requires justification or consent)
Corporation / Limited where inconsistent with the proposed entity type
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 15 business days of a name-rejection notice, the applicant through its Registered Agent may file a written reconsideration request with the Registrar of Corporations in Majuro. The request must cite the distinguishing features under § 103 of the Business Corporations Act, identify any prior-user consent obtained, and include the administrative reconsideration fee of USD 50. If the Registrar affirms the rejection, the applicant may reserve an alternative name or commence judicial review before the High Court of the Marshall Islands within 30 days under the Administrative Procedure Act.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A non-resident Business Corporation must continuously maintain both a registered office and a licensed Registered Agent in the Marshall Islands. The statutory registered office is the physical address of the Registered Agent in Majuro; the corporation itself may conduct all operations remotely with no physical premises in RMI, and virtual-office substitutes that replace the statutory Registered Agent are not permissible. For this cloud cybersecurity SaaS business, the virtual service address arrangement through the Registered Agent is fully compliant.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low — estimated <5% per annum for unannounced physical inspection of the Business Corporation's own premises, because the entity has no physical office, employees, or assets in the Marshall Islands. The Registered Agent's office in Majuro, however, carries a moderate likelihood (estimated 10–20% per annum) of inspection by the Registrar of Corporations or the FIU for AML/CFT supervision and corporate-registry compliance.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance and corporate name reservation fee under Business Corporations Act § 103
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Ministry of Finance, Republic of the Marshall Islands
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory government tariff (official Registry fee schedule)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Government incorporation filing fee for a Business Corporation with authorized share capital up to USD 50,000
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Ministry of Finance, Republic of the Marshall Islands

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certificate of Incorporation and five certified true copies for banking and Stripe/KYC onboarding
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Ministry of Finance, Republic of the Marshall Islands

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Licensed Registered Agent retainer for year one, including registered office in Majuro, statutory agent consent, and regulatory correspondence handling
Articles of Incorporation and Bylaws drafting, corporate resolutions, UBO-structure legal review, and Stage 1 due-diligence memos by external counsel
Beneficial Ownership Statement filing and internal UBO register setup at the 25% ownership threshold
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registered Agent on behalf of the Registrar of Corporations
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory compliance fee plus agent administrative charge

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PEP, OFAC, UN and EU sanctions screening and AML/CFT CDD file compilation for all directors, shareholders and UBOs
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registered Agent / Money Laundering Reporting Officer (MLRO) compliance function

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and/or consular legalization bundle for the notarized incorporation folder (up to five documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: RMI Ministry of Foreign Affairs / origin-country Apostille authority or consulate

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Marshall Islands Business Corporations Act (Title 10, Revised Code of the Marshall Islands), Sections 10-201 (Execution of Articles), 10-210 (Certificate of Incorporation), 10-310 (Registered Office and Agent), 10-401 (Board of Directors), and 10-501 (Share Issuance); supplemented by the Registrar of Corporations Procedural Rules
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Business Registry Division, Office of the Attorney General, Delap-Uliga-Djarrit, Majuro, Republic of the Marshall Islands
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form BC-1) filed pursuant to Section 10-201 of the Business Corporations Act
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; issued capital may be nominal (US$1 per issued share or par value). Consideration may consist of cash, services, promissory notes, or tangible/intangible property. No escrow account or capital deposit is required by the Registrar for a non-resident Business Corporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Corporation hereby accepts the subscription of authorized shares from the incorporators and issues such ordinary shares for lawful consideration as recorded in the share subscription register; RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the Corporation shall be established and continuously maintained with the licensed registered agent in the Marshall Islands, and the agent is appointed to accept service of process; RESOLVED FURTHER, that the following persons be and hereby are appointed officers of the Corporation: President, Secretary, and Treasurer, each with authority to open bank accounts, execute contracts, and file statutory returns; RESOLVED FURTHER, that such officers may delegate administrative tasks to the registered agent and are directed to complete all governance and licensing filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Clearance and Preliminary Availability Search
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Business Registry Division, Office of the Attorney General, Majuro (online search tool and counter service)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the corporate name 'as proposed' via Form NR-1 or through the licensed formation agent's portal. The Registrar verifies that the name is distinguishable from existing registered names, does not imply a regulated banking or government purpose, and complies with Section 10-204. Upon approval, the name is reserved for 30 days. If signed outside the Marshall Islands, applicant identity documents must be notarized and apostilled in accordance with the Hague Apostille Convention.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application (Form NR-1)
Passport copy of each incorporator (notarized)
Power of attorney to the licensed formation agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused as confusingly similar or impermissible, submit up to three alternate names within 5 business days; a written administrative review may be requested with the Registrar within 30 days of refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporator's execution before a notary public; licensed registered agent acts as witness and liaison
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation (Form BC-1) stating corporate name, registered agent identity, registered office address in Majuro, authorized share structure, and permitted business purpose (ISIC 6201 computer programming and related cybersecurity services). Execute the document before a notary; if executed abroad, apply for an Apostille certificate from the competent authority of the jurisdiction of execution. The initial registered agent must countersign the consent section.
required_dossiers: Duly executed Articles of Incorporation (Form BC-1)
Consent of registered agent
Draft Bylaws (to be filed with corporate records)
Share subscription memorandum
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries defective provisions (e.g., lawful-use purpose clause, unauthorized share designations), the formation agent shall amend and re-execute the Articles within 14 business days without additional statutory fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Filing and Fee Settlement with the Registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Business Registry Division, Office of the Attorney General, Majuro (in-person counter or authorized licensed agent filing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed and apostilled Articles of Incorporation together with the US$275 filing fee (or US$350 for expedited processing). Payment is accepted by certified bank check, wire transfer, or through the registered agent's prepaid account. The Registrar stamps the filing and assigns a corporate registration number. The certificate of incorporation is generated on approval.
required_dossiers: Original Articles of Incorporation (with Apostille if executed abroad)
Proof of payment of the statutory filing fee
Covering letter from the licensed formation agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is rejected, cure the deficiencies identified in the Registrar's written rejection notice and re-file within 14 days; a written appeal lies to the Attorney General, and expedited re-examination may be purchased at the statutory surcharge rate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Appointment of Registered Agent and Designation of Registered Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Business Registry Division (registered agent licensing); agent located in Majuro, Republic of the Marshall Islands
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the registered agent consent letter and designate the agent's physical address (not a P.O. box) as the registered office. The agent must be an individual resident of the Marshall Islands or a licensed corporate services company. The agent is responsible for receiving service of process, government notices, and annual franchise tax reminders. The registered office is effective from the date the Articles are filed.
required_dossiers: Registered agent consent letter (countersigned)
Registered office address confirmation slip
Letter of authorization from the board of directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the agent's consent is absent or defective, the Registrar will reject the Articles; cure by obtaining a fresh executed consent and filing the same within 10 days. A change of agent may be made by board resolution filed on Form BC-2.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of Bylaws and Approval of First Board Resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Corporation; minutes retained at the registered office and with the formation agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the inaugural board meeting or obtain unanimous written consent. Adopt the Bylaws, approve the pro-forma First Board Resolution (share issuance, registered office adoption, officer appointments), open the share ledger, and issue share certificates. Officers shall execute banking forms for the corporate bank account and confirm the KYC file with the banks. This step is recorded in the corporate records book maintained by the registered agent.
required_dossiers: Adopted Bylaws
Signed First Board Resolution (unanimous written consent)
Acceptance of office letters from the President, Secretary, and Treasurer
Share certificate ledger and specimen certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Bylaws or resolutions conflict with the Business Corporations Act, the board shall adopt conforming amendments by unanimous written consent and record the same with the registered agent; no public filing is required for internal governance documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Business Registry Division, Office of the Attorney General, Majuro
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon registration, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation bearing the corporate seal, registration number, and date of filing. The company may then request a Certificate of Good Standing (often used for bank account opening and SaaS vendor onboarding). Verify that the registered name, authorized shares, and registered agent details match the final corporate record before ordering certified copies.
required_dossiers: Stamped copy of the executed Articles of Incorporation
Registrar's certificate issuance order
Irrevocable instruction letter specifying officer identities for the Good Standing certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is delayed beyond the service standard, the applicant may request an expedited certified draft from the Deputy Registrar or petition the High Court for a writ of mandamus compelling issuance under the Business Corporations Act.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Business License Office, Ministry of Finance, Republic of the Marshall Islands (and the municipality where the physical office is located)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Business License (General Commercial Services) issued under the Business License Act 2002, as amended

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority of the Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI EPA)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B - Registration / Categorical Exemption: the cloud-based SaaS activity is exempt from a full EIA under the RMI Environmental Impact Assessment Regulations 1989 because it involves no construction, manufacturing, or discharge-generating physical undertaking; a simple operational registration notice with the RMI EPA is sufficient before the business license is issued.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero industrial point-source wastewater discharge; office premises must connect to municipal sewage or a RMI EPA-approved septic system, with effluent meeting the RMI EPA surface-water standards (pH 6.0 to 8.5, BOD less than 30 mg/L, TSS less than 50 mg/L). No VOC or stack emission thresholds are triggered by IT operations. All decommissioned servers and electronic waste must be disposed through RMI EPA-approved recycling contractors; no hazardous waste stream is generated by the software activity.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Compliance Certificate from the local Municipal Fire and Rescue Division covering extinguishers, emergency egress, and alarm systems; structural load inspection certificate of the leased office from a registered civil engineer; and an occupational safety clearance issued by the Ministry of Health and Human Services (WORKSAFE RMI) confirming compliance with workplace ergonomic, ventilation, and electrical safety baselines.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Tax and Revenue Division, Ministry of Finance, Banking and Postal Services, Republic of the Marshall Islands (official portal: https://finance.gov.mh; corporate registration is administered by the RMI Registrar of Corporations through licensed registered agents, accessible via the Corporations Registry online entity search system)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate a Business Corporation under the Business Corporations Act 1990 through a licensed RMI registered agent; the Registrar issues a Certificate of Incorporation and a Corporate Registration Number (CRN), which is the primary entity identifier for all tax, banking, and compliance purposes. Step 2: If the corporation files the Non-Resident Domestic Corporation (NRDC) election and conducts no business within the Republic, no Marshall Islands income tax or gross revenue tax TIN is required; the CRN together with the NRDC certificate constitutes the full statutory tax identity. Step 3: If the corporation later hires RMI-resident employees, register with the RMI Social Security Administration for an employer contribution account and with the Tax and Revenue Division for wage-tax withholding; a payroll-based employer TIN will then be assigned. Step 4: Pay the annual corporate franchise tax of USD 250 (base amount, tiered by authorized capital) and maintain the registered agent's annual renewal filing to keep the tax-exempt NRDC status in good standing.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone (Marshall Islands non-resident domestic corporation deriving no Marshall Islands-source revenue and conducting no business within the Republic is exempt from RMI income tax and the 3% gross revenue tax; the RMI applies a territorial/source-based tax system and imposes no VAT, no capital gains tax, no net worth tax, and no withholding tax on non-residents)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: The only relevant RMI statutory election is the Non-Resident Domestic Corporation (NRDC) designation under the Business Corporations Act 1990, filed by the registered agent at incorporation or by later amendment; it conclusively places the entity outside the RMI tax base. RMI law has no check-the-box regime, no CFC election, and no hybrid mismatch election. A U.S. federal check-the-box election (IRS Form 8832) may be filed if the corporation becomes a U.S. tax payer or derives U.S.-source income, but that election is purely a U.S. federal tax classification and is not recognized by RMI tax law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: None -- the Republic of the Marshall Islands does not operate a VAT, GST, or sales-and-use tax. The indirect revenue instruments in force are limited to customs import duties (Customs Tariff Act 1995), fuel tax, and the Green Tax departure levy. Cloud vulnerability scanning and penetration-testing SaaS exports are intangible services and have no Marshall Islands indirect tax nexus.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable - no VAT/GST registration threshold exists in RMI law (the official currency is the United States dollar). A customs importer licence or excise registration is required only for physical importation of tangible goods into the Republic; SaaS services are delivered digitally from outside RMI customs territory and do not trigger any registration threshold. A non-resident domestic corporation has no indirect tax registration duty.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No electronic invoicing, real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or tax-authority API mandate exists in the Marshall Islands for SaaS or other services. Physical-goods customs declarations are processed electronically through UNCTAD ASYCUDA World; intangible service invoices require only ordinary commercial invoice standards. No government seal, hash code, or fiscal watermark is required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable -- because the RMI imposes no VAT/GST, there is no export zero-rating certificate, no export VAT refund, and no claim procedure. The cross-border SaaS supply (cloud vulnerability scanning and penetration testing) constitutes foreign-source revenue outside the RMI gross revenue tax base and outside the customs framework. Documentation that the customer is located abroad and that no performance occurs in the RMI is nevertheless recommended to preserve the NRDC exemption and to satisfy the registered agent's AML/KYC duties.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Corporate Registration Number and NRDC certificate issued by the RMI Registrar of Corporations (primary tax identity evidence)
Commercial master services agreement and penetration-testing scope/deliverable documents evidencing offshore service delivery
Invoice and payment evidence (Stripe payout reports or wire transfer advices) with inward remittance records maintained under the registered agent's AML/KYC file
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The RMI has no VAT export-fraud clawback regime because no VAT exists. However, abusive use of the NRDC status (e.g., conducting RMI-source business while claiming non-resident exemption) triggers reassessment under the Gross Revenue Tax Act and the Income Tax Act, with penalties of up to 25% for non-fraudulent underpayment and up to 50% plus imprisonment exposure for fraudulent evasion, together with revocation of the corporate licence by the Registrar and director liability under the Business Corporations Act. If the SaaS exporter claims zero-rating in a foreign VAT jurisdiction (such as the EU, Australia, or U.S. states), any fraudulent claim remains subject to that foreign jurisdiction's interest, penalty, and clawback rules.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banking Commissioner, Ministry of Finance, Republic of the Marshall Islands (the RMI has no domestic central bank; the official currency is the United States Dollar and monetary policy is effectively determined by the U.S. Federal Reserve)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The United States Dollar is the sole legal tender in the Marshall Islands, and the RMI does not operate exchange controls or require approvals for current or capital account transactions. Profit remittances and dividends may be paid freely in USD through RMI chartered banks, but originating banks may require standard source-of-funds documentation, beneficial ownership disclosure, and, where the payor is a domestic RMI bank account holder, a tax clearance certificate or representation from the business corporation confirming no outstanding RMI statutory liabilities.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory export proceeds surrender requirements under the laws of the Marshall Islands. A non-resident business corporation may retain 100% of export or SaaS subscription receipts in USD in any licensed bank account, without mandatory conversion, waiting period, foreign exchange authorization, or surrender certification.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of Guam - Marshall Islands Branch

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium with legal constraints. The RMI does not have a domestic electronic money institution or EMI licensing framework. Offshore digital EMIs (e.g. Stripe Treasury-like platforms, Wise Business, or licensed EU/UK/SG payment institutions) may be used as auxiliary collection or disbursement rails for SaaS subscription revenue, provided the EMI holds a valid license in its home jurisdiction and meets RMI AML/KYC expectations. Offshore EMIs cannot act as the primary or sole RMI treasury account, and funds held with an unlicensed EMI are not bank deposits protected under RMI banking law or the U.S. Federal Deposit Insurance regime.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: RMI chartered banks generally require at least one director or authorized signatory to attend an in-person or compliance interview with a bank officer before account activation. Remote opening may be considered on a case-by-case basis, particularly for non-resident corporations, but only with apostilled corporate documents, notarized board resolutions, certified passport copies, and a pre-arranged video interview approved by the bank's money laundering compliance officer. A physical registered agent in the Marshall Islands and a clear corporate ownership schedule are mandatory prerequisites.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident Business Corporation lacking local physical office or economic substance in RMI
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered agent certificate; certified articles of incorporation and bylaws; board resolution authorizing account opening; directors and shareholders register; corporate organizational chart; proof of business activity (SaaS contracts, penetration testing engagement letters); annual financial statements; and a written substance-and-linkage statement explaining the use of the RMI entity in the cross-border cybersecurity commerce structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity, nominee-shareholder arrangements, or bearer-share exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Up-to-date beneficial ownership register; full natural-person details for all ultimate beneficial owners; signed declarations of no bearer shares; legal opinion or certified extract from the RMI Registrar confirming no bearer instruments are outstanding; and sworn source-of-wealth statements for each 25%-or-greater owner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume cyber SaaS cross-border subscription inflows with short entity operating history
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited or reviewed financial statements; a realistic treasury projection model showing expected subscription and disbursement volumes; customer contracts and invoicing records; a detailed list of counterparties and payment corridors; procurement/disbursement policies; and a board-adopted AML/CFT compliance manual adapted to the business's low inherent risk tier.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, PEP, adverse-media, or jurisdiction-screening hits on owners, directors, or counterparties
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Clear beneficial-owner and officer passport scans; certified birth certificates or equivalent identity documents; independent sanctions/PEP screening reports for each relevant jurisdiction (UN, OFAC, EU, UK, FATF); corporate records containing original disqualification/criminal-record declarations; and an explanation statement supported by corroborating legal or financial documents where any name similarity or red-flag hit is resolved.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route the capital injection via SWIFT MT103 from the originating bank to the RMI chartered bank's correspondent account, using a clear USD credit path through the U.S. clearing network (Fedwire or correspondent bank). The payment narrative must identify the sender, the receiving business corporation MH_BC, the purpose as 'capital contribution' or 'paid-in capital increase', and reference the corporate registration number. The RMI bank will verify the ultimate originator, source-of-funds documentation, board authorization, and the beneficiary's beneficial ownership schedule. Because no RMI exchange control exists, no central bank pre-approval is required; however, the bank may request a board resolution, updated shareholder register, and a source-of-wealth statement for funds exceeding internal thresholds.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use USD-denominated SWIFT MT103 for direct fund transfers to vendors, contractors, and SaaS infrastructure providers; use MT103/MT202 for correspondent bank transfers involving non-USD settlement. For large technology procurement or infrastructure licensing, instruct the issuing RMI bank to open an irrevocable commercial letter of credit via SWIFT MT700 with the beneficiary bank, ensuring U.S. or internationally recognized governing rules (UCP600). For smaller recurring cloud services, ACH payments or SWIFT global payments initiative (gpi) transfers are appropriate. All disbursements under the enterprise treasury policy require documentary evidence of the commercial/subscription purpose and a valid invoice or contract reference.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/AUD and USD/EUR deliverable FX forward contracts
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in restricted Asian and African currencies for cross-border SaaS trade settlement exposure
Standard FX swaps for liquidity management of USD receivables vs. offshore vendor payables
Cross-currency swaps for major capital purchases or long-term infrastructure procurement in non-USD currencies

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Report and Corporation License Renewal (base fee tier for authorized capital up to USD 50,000)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Marshall Islands Corporate Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the annual anniversary of the corporation's date of incorporation; the renewal window opens 60 days prior and closes on the anniversary itself.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 10% of the unpaid annual fee accrues for each month or partial month of delay, capped at 100% of the base fee. Persistent default beyond 3 months authorizes the Registrar to administratively dissolve the corporation; reinstatement thereafter requires payment of all outstanding fees, accumulated penalties, and a reinstatement filing fee.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory statutory audit is imposed on a non-resident Marshall Islands Business Corporation. An independent audit is triggered only where (i) shareholders holding at least 10% of the voting capital demand one, (ii) the company is listed on a securities exchange, or (iii) it undertakes regulated activity requiring a financial statement audit under the Banking Act or Trust Company Act.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: The Marshall Islands Business Corporations Act does not mandate a specific accounting framework. Non-resident corporations may maintain records under IFRS, US GAAP, or the simplified local GAAP in the Company's home jurisdiction. Financial statements are not required to be filed with the Registrar and may be kept at the registered office or principal place of business.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Marshall Islands AML/CFT legal framework, the appointed registered agent must hold current beneficial ownership evidence. Annually, within 30 days after the corporation's anniversary filing date, each non-resident shareholder or ultimate beneficial owner must submit a signed written confirmation to the registered agent re-affirming the shareholding list, ownership percentages, and any change in control. In addition, any share transfer during the year must be reported to the registered agent within 14 days of the transfer being recorded. This confirmation is retained by the registered agent and is not filed with the public Registrar.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,200 – USD 2,500 per annum inclusive of registered office services, registered agent representation, corporate records custody, and lodging of the annual report.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 – USD 15,000 per annum (only applicable if a shareholder-requested or commercially required independent audit is engaged; not a standard annual cost for the non-resident entity).

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Non-Resident Business Corporations enjoy a complete statutory exemption from corporate income tax, capital gains tax, and withholding tax on distributions. The only recurrent fiscal levy is the annual franchise fee (authorized-capital based) payable to the RMI Registrar of Corporations. A 3% Gross Revenue Tax applies exclusively to persons conducting commercial activity within the RMI; an inactive non-resident BC is outside that charge.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: No corporate income tax return is prescribed for a Non-Resident Business Corporation. The sole annual statutory compliance filing is the Business Corporation Annual Report (Form BC-AR), filed through the RMI Registrar of Corporations online system at www.rmioc.gov.mh.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The Annual Report must be filed on or before 31 March each year in respect of the preceding calendar year. There is no corporate income tax filing deadline because no corporate income tax return is due.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box A: Corporate Name and Registration Number
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exact legal name and RMI corporate registration number as recorded in the Certificate of Incorporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the certified English legal name exactly and the numeric registration identifier; do not include trade names or abbreviations unless previously amended.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box B: Registered Agent and Registered Office
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Physical street address of the RMI licensed registered agent and the statutory registered office in the Republic of the Marshall Islands.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident BC cannot designate an address outside the RMI; the registered agent must be a licensed RMI resident agent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annual confirmation that the corporation is not engaged in trade or business within the RMI, derives no RMI-source revenue, and maintains no office, employees, or assets in the RMI.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A director or the registered agent must affirm this declaration. False certification is a statutory offence and removes the BC from the zero-tax category.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 2: Authorized Share Capital and Franchise Fee Schedule
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Schedule of authorized shares, par value, share classes, and computation of the annual franchise fee.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter share classes exactly as in the Articles of Incorporation; an unauthorized change invalidates the filing and exposes the company to penalty.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the Annual Report incurs a US$500 penalty plus a monthly surcharge of US$50 per month or part thereof. Failure to file and pay for two consecutive years results in administrative dissolution by the Registrar. Reinstatement requires payment of all arrearages, a 10% reinstatement surcharge, and a new Certificate of Good Standing. No late corporate income tax return penalty is applicable because no such return exists for an RMI non-resident BC.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The Marshall Islands has no comprehensive double taxation agreement in force for corporate income tax purposes. A Non-Resident Business Corporation cannot invoke treaty relief because it is not an RMI income-tax resident and does not receive an RMI Tax Residency Certificate. RMI law imposes zero withholding on dividend distributions to shareholders, so no domestic relief mechanism is required. If a foreign counterparty erroneously withholds on payments to the BC, the company may produce its Certificate of Non-Resident Status or the Annual Report declaration to evidence tax-exempt non-resident standing.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding tax on royalties and interest paid to non-residents is 0% in the RMI. No treaty rate exists given the absence of any applicable DTA. Therefore, payments for cybersecurity SaaS licenses, cloud penetration testing service fees, and intercompany debt interest are not subject to RMI withholding tax.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No statutory transfer pricing threshold exists in the RMI. The RMI Income Tax Act and Business Corporations Act do not mandate Local File or Master File documentation. As a defensive international compliance measure, contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation is recommended only when the consolidated group turnover exceeds US$50,000,000 or the group operates in jurisdictions applying OECD BEPS Action 13 rules. The same file can substantiate arm's length pricing if a foreign tax authority recharacterizes the RMI entity.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The RMI has not enacted Economic Substance Regulations comparable to the BVI or the Cayman Islands. No statutory economic substance test is imposed on a Non-Resident Business Corporation. However, because the entity is a zero-tax cybersecurity SaaS provider, foreign revenue authorities may examine the arrangement under CFC rules, controlled-foreign-company legislation, or substance-over-form doctrines (e.g., U.S. Section 482, U.K. CFC rules, OECD Pillar Two income inclusion). The BC should maintain demonstrable commercial reality: board minutes documenting strategic decisions, executed client contracts, actual billing flows through USD accounts, and evidence of security-service delivery capability outside the RMI. A brass-plate structure with artificial risk allocation will be disregarded by foreign tax courts despite the absence of RMI ESR.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Certifying a non-resident declaration while in fact conducting commercial activity inside the Marshall Islands, such as physically performing penetration testing on an RMI government network, maintaining a local office, employing local personnel, or executing contracts with RMI-source revenue, thereby evading the 3% Gross Revenue Tax and the annual franchise fee.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Retroactive assessment of 3% Gross Revenue Tax on all RMI-source gross receipts, plus statutory interest and penalties of up to 25% of the deficiency. The false declaration is punishable by a fine of up to US$10,000 and imprisonment for up to five years under RMI criminal law. The Registrar may cancel the non-resident exemption certificate and strike the company from the register.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who knowingly execute the false declaration are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid Gross Revenue Tax, interest, and penalties. RMI courts may pierce the corporate veil under common-law fraud doctrine, impose civil restitution orders, and issue travel bans or passport surrenders where assets are dissipated outside the jurisdiction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Forming an RMI BC solely to isolate Cybersecurity SaaS revenue while all actual management, personnel, product development, and client-facing operations occur in another country, with no RMI board meetings, no segregated books, no registered-agent awareness of commercial activity, and no business purpose other than tax avoidance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Registrar may dissolve the corporation for failure to maintain a valid registered agent or for filing false Annual Reports. In civil proceedings, the RMI corporate personality will be disregarded as a sham; all contracts executed through the shell become personally enforceable against the beneficial owner. Affirmative misuse of the shell constitutes common-law fraud and may result in disqualification of the entity from appearing before RMI courts until dissolution is reversed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and shareholders who use the shell to obstruct creditors or to conceal the true principal are personally liable for all corporate trade debts and contractual obligations. RMI courts may impose asset-disclosure orders, travel bans, and monetary penalties; directors convicted of fraudulent misrepresentation face imprisonment of up to five years and permanent exclusion from serving as directors of RMI corporations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting Stripe subscription payments and wire transfers without performing customer due diligence, maintaining no five-year transactional records, failing to verify beneficial ownership, or processing payments for sanctioned entities and ransomware-affiliated clients using the RMI BC as an opaque invoicing gateway.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under RMI anti-money laundering legislation, each predicate violation is punishable by a fine of up to US$75,000 and imprisonment for up to fourteen years. The RMI Financial Intelligence Unit may freeze corporate bank accounts, issue suspicious transaction reporting directives, and obtain civil forfeiture of the SaaS subscription revenue. The Registrar may revoke the certificate of incorporation as an instrumentality of money laundering.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers designated as persons in charge of AML controls may be prosecuted individually even though the acts occurred within the corporate form. RMI courts may impose disgorgement from personal accounts, confiscation of travel documents, travel bans pending trial, and enhanced monitoring. Beneficial owners directing the payment scheme remain criminally liable as principals.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Structuring intercompany SaaS license resale arrangements so that the RMI shell invoices the end client at a 15–20% markup while all cybersecurity development, cloud infrastructure, and support functions remain in a high-tax jurisdiction, with no RMI personnel and no transfer pricing study, and thereafter issuing invoices referencing a fictional RMI tax residency or DTA with the client's country.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The client's tax authority will apply controlled-foreign-company or arm's length recharacterization, allocate all profit to the developer jurisdiction, disallow the RMI invoice as a deduction, and impose interest and accuracy-related penalties ranging from 20% to 40% of the understatement. The RMI Registrar may dissolve the BC after an exchange-of-information request discloses false Annual Report certificates. Unsupported treaty claims may expose the signatory to criminal liability for tax fraud in the foreign jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly approve misleading invoices or false substance declarations may be held personally liable for the resulting tax assessment in foreign proceedings. U.S. CFC and anti-avoidance enforcement can extend the fraud limitation period, impose personal monetary penalties on individuals, and provoke passport revocation or travel restrictions. Deriving personal benefit from the artificial margin triggers piercing of the RMI corporate veil and general creditor claims against the director's personal assets.
